text:
anya: Quick sync — I’m drafting the PRD/spec for the docs-as-spec quickstart and examples we promised to the pilot customers. Need to converge on acceptance criteria, edge cases to call out, and a minimal e2e quickstart snippet that we can run in CI. Customer asks to show hosted + dedicated + private flows, model pin + automatic fallback behavior, and rollback steps.

matt: +1. Also add perf SLOs and a cost-guardrail section (how to avoid runaway batch sizes / token spend). Can we define a default batching policy in the quickstart? :thinking_face:?

sara: I can draft the quickstart + examples. Question: do we want the snippet to use the Console-first flow (token config + route) or the SDK-first flow? SDK-first is easier for devs but Console flow shows prod ops.

tyler: Edge-case list (short bullets): KV cache invalidation on model switch, prefix-caching with long context (>8k), quantized-vs-fp model outputs mismatch, tool-calling failure when function schema changes, and network partition fallbacks. We should list graceful degradation per case.

anya: Proposed acceptance criteria (pickable):
- AC1: Quickstart repo runs end-to-end in CI (creates route, deploys model variant, runs sample prompts, asserts outputs match golden set)
- AC2: Examples cover all 3 deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private) with clear config snippets for each
- AC3: Rollback/canary documented: how to pin model, canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%, automatic fallback to safe model on error
- AC4: Perf SLOs included: p95 latency targets (example: p95 < 300ms for short prompts, < 800ms for 2k tokens on dedicated at baseline traffic) and token-cost estimation guidance
- AC5: Security note: KMS usage and redaction in quickstart logs for private deployments

matt: Those ACs look solid. I’d add an explicit test for "fallback on OOM or kernel mismatch" so the quickstart demonstrates the fallback path. Also add a small perf harness we can run in CI to check p95, maybe with a tiny load generator.

ci-bot: CI: example-quickstart lint passed (job #432). :white_check_mark:

sara: Draft snippet — SDK-first minimal example (will add comments for Console variants):
```
# python quickstart (minimal)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
rc = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_KEY}")
route = rc.routes.create(name="quickstart-sample", model="redwood/small-1:2026-03-01", deployment_mode="hosted")
resp = rc.generate(route=route.id, prompt="Summarize the README in one sentence")
print(resp.text)
```
I’ll add variants for dedicated/private and a YAML Console snippet next.

tyler: For edge cases in the doc, can we include a short section: "If output diverges after quantization": steps = (1) compare logits on small input, (2) pin to fp model, (3) file bug with model-onboarding. Keeps customers from chasing ghosts.

matt: I’ll create a perf test ticket and canary matrix — assigning to @matt and @tyler. Also adding a short checklist item: "example quickstart must pass example smoke test on both Linux and macOS runners".

anya: Action items / owners — can we lock EOW?
- sara: quickstart draft + hosted/dedicated/private examples (owner)
- matt: perf harness + canary matrix + CI jobs (owner)
- tyler: edge-case appendix + fallback playbook (owner)

sara: I’ll do the draft and link PR by EOD Friday. :+1:

matt: I’ll post the perf ticket and rough matrix by tomorrow.

anya: Great — once we have the PR I’ll do an internal review and then we can run the CI smoke. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
